recommendation: Exclude 1.61; central should be ~0.03-0.05 direct

issue: Hydrogen is a listed carrier but there is no [hydrogen] SEC; hydrocracking consumes 2-4 wt% H2 (3-6 GJ/t) - the largest energy flow of the unit - so the model would see no H2 demand.
benchmark: Hydrocracker H2 make-up 200-400 Nm3/t ~ 2.5-5 GJ/t; HDS 20-100 Nm3/t
recommendation: Add [hydrogen] SEC from REF BREF / Worrell 2015

issue: 0.548 GJ/t fuel implies 0.031 t/t; combustion central is half that (different example sets).
recommendation: Accept; note mismatch

issue: Central (REF BREF, top-ranked) sits at the top of the range and above the archetype's own description (400-800 MJ/t).
benchmark: REF BREF 2015: visbreaker 400-800 MJ/t fuel; Energetics: ~80 kBtu/bbl ~ 0.6 GJ/t
recommendation: Use ~0.6 GJ/t (mid of BREF range); the 0.92 may be the soaker+vacuum-flasher configuration

issue: Same unit confusion as autothermal-reformer: product declared t but labelled GJ; capacity 402 kt/yr is an ammonia plant (BREF), capex/opex from Collodi 2010 are an H2 plant, SEC 31.1 GJ/t (10.3-68.4) pools per-t-NH3 totals with unknown bases. The archetype is an efficiency measure yet carries absolute consumption and whole-plant lifetime.
benchmark: Ammonia SMR 28-35 GJ/t NH3; H2 ~170-190 GJ/t; measure savings 5-10%
recommendation: Re-base to GJ H2 and store the measure as a saving (or an SEC multiplier) with incremental capex; drop the ammonia-plant capacity

issue: Untagged total is below the [natural-gas] carrier (1.23) - impossible; min example 0.00932 is an electricity-only value pooled as total.
benchmark: SMR total ~1.3-1.45 GJ/GJ HHV (NETL 2022: 1.32)
recommendation: Exclude the 0.00932 example; total should equal NG+elec ~1.25-1.45

issue: Central at the minimum of its range and inconsistent with SEC [natural-gas] 1.23 GJ/GJ (81%); 85% is an LHV or feed-only value.
recommendation: Use ~74-76%; check LHV/HHV on the 85 example

issue: Central ~580 USD/kW_H2, about 35% below IEA's reference but within the literature band for large merchant SMRs.
benchmark: IEA 2019: 910 USD/kW_H2 (-> ~39 CAD/GJ-per-yr); NETL 2022 ~700-900 USD/kW
recommendation: Accept; note low-side

issue: Central matches 9 t CO2/t H2; min 0.0317 is half (feed-only or LHV-per-kg slip) and max 0.101 is ~14 t/t H2 (includes upstream?).
recommendation: Accept central; check the two extremes' scope

issue: Captured 0.0564 + residual 0.03 = 0.086 t/GJ, above the unabated 0.064-0.07; captured implies 83% capture while share-to-capture (60%) and residual (0.03) imply ~55-60%. Examples with flue-gas capture (90%+, e.g. H2A-Lite 96.3%) are pooled into the shift-gas-only archetype.
benchmark: Shift-gas capture 55-65% of plant CO2 (IEAGHG 2017-02 case 2A); shift+flue 90%+
recommendation: Move >85% share-to-capture examples to the ccs-diffuse (or combined) archetype; recompute captured as share x unabated

issue: Untagged 96.3 is a full-flue capture configuration, not shift-gas-only.
recommendation: Re-assign to ccs-diffuse

issue: Pembina life-cycle figure includes upstream methane; it is larger than the direct CO2 central (0.03) and not comparable to the direct-emission rows.
benchmark: Gorski 2021 (Pembina): blue H2 50-60 g CO2e/MJ LHV life-cycle
recommendation: Tag as life-cycle or drop

issue: Scope: ETSAP 2011 figure is a whole liquefaction plant, not the GT refrigeration drive; also low versus post-2012 project costs.
benchmark: IGU/Oxford 2020: liquefaction 800-1,500 USD/tpa (US brownfield) to 3,000+ (Australia) -> 1,100-2,000+ CAD/t-per-yr
recommendation: Move to liquefaction-train_base-load; if kept for the drive, use ~25-35% of plant cost

issue: Fuel use 5-6% of LNG energy content is at the efficient end; GT-driven base-load trains typically burn 8-12% of feed (4.5-6.5 GJ/t).
benchmark: IGU, Shell: 8-12% of feed gas for GT-driven liquefaction
recommendation: Accept but note low-side; the [not-stated] 0.9-1.4 GJ/t is shaft work (250-380 kWh/t), not fuel - tag it

issue: Max 18.3 GJ/t is a third of LNG's energy content - too high even for small-scale (max ~15%, i.e. 8 GJ/t); likely a kWh/t to GJ/t or per-m3 slip.
benchmark: Small-scale: 500-900 kWh/t shaft = 1.8-3.2 GJ/t electricity, or 6-8 GJ/t gas if GT/engine driven
recommendation: Re-check the 18.3 example; tag the [not-stated] 1.79 GJ/t as electricity (500 kWh/t)

issue: The [ch4]-tagged abatement costs across this and the other methane archetypes (dry-gas-seal -232, VRU -68, LDAR 325, plunger 260) are ~25x the [co2e]-tagged ones, i.e. they are per t CH4, not per t CO2e as labelled.
benchmark: -152/25 = -6 CAD/t CO2e, matching the co2e central
recommendation: Re-unit the [ch4] abatement costs (divide by 25 or 28) or relabel unit as CAD/t CH4; apply to all methane archetypes

issue: O&M at 46% of capex per year: plausible only because blowdown recovery is a rented-compressor/labour practice; flag so the opex/capex sanity check does not trip.
benchmark: Natural Gas STAR: portable recompression ~USD 1-2/Mcf recovered
recommendation: Accept; note practice-type cost

issue: Low versus STAR: a dry-seal retrofit ~USD 300-400k saves ~40-50 MMcf/yr (800-950 t) -> ~400 USD/t-yr -> 550-800 CAD/t-yr in 2025 CAD; the 852 example is the STAR-consistent one. Rod-packing replacement (~USD 5-10k per 10-20 t/yr) is similar.
benchmark: EPA Natural Gas STAR Lessons Learned (wet seals -> dry seals): 300-400 USD per t/yr saved
recommendation: Check whether the 82-120 examples are incremental (seal replacement at overhaul) and tag; otherwise prefer ~500-800

issue: = ~4,100 USD/kW if GJ is shaft output; high versus motor-driven compressor packages but possible with substation/line; if GJ is gas throughput energy it is ~x30 too high.
benchmark: E-drive compressor station 1,500-2,500 USD/kW installed shaft
recommendation: Confirm the GJ denominator (shaft vs throughput)

issue: 150M CAD for a 100 kt CO2/yr (~36 kt gas) recovery unit is x3-5 the usual refinery FGR package (USD 10-30M); drives the abatement-cost central to 71 CAD/t when literature puts FGR at negative to ~40 CAD/t.
benchmark: World Bank GGFR / refinery FGR: 10-30 USD/t CO2 or cost-negative with gas credit
recommendation: Re-check N-ZIP basis (may include compression to pipeline/export); add STAR/Clearstone FGR examples

issue: capex 1.97 CAD/m3-per-yr x capacity 103 Mm3/yr = 203M CAD - impossible for an instrument-air system (USD 50-100k). The capex and opex are per m3 CH4 avoided (~2,900 CAD per t CH4/yr), the capacity is facility gas throughput.
benchmark: STAR: instrument air USD 30-100k saving 10-30 MMcf/yr (200-600 t) -> 100-500 USD/t-yr
recommendation: Re-base product to t CH4 avoided (like the other vent measures); recompute capacity

issue: Max 10,379 is a unit/denominator error; instrument air is one of the cheapest measures (RIAS: <10 CAD/t).
benchmark: ECCC 2018 RIAS, ICF 2015: -5 to +10 CAD/t CO2e
recommendation: Exclude the 10,379 example

issue: VRUs are usually cost-negative to low-cost because recovered gas/NGL is sold; 45 CAD/t is the high end and the top-ranked source is a 1999 study.
benchmark: ICF 2015 / RIAS: -10 to +15 CAD/t CO2e for VRUs
recommendation: Add a Clearstone/ICF example; central capex 235 and opex 48 CAD/t-yr are consistent with STAR

issue: Dehydrator is the incumbent; a 90% reduction belongs to a measure (flash-tank separator / circulation optimization / desiccant), not the base technology.
benchmark: STAR LL: flash tank separators recover ~90% of glycol-pump vented gas
recommendation: Move to a measure archetype or drop

issue: Unclear what temperature this is: TEG reboiler runs 190-200 degC, contactor 30-45 degC; 93 degC (200 degF) matches neither.
benchmark: GPSA: TEG reboiler 175-204 degC
recommendation: Check Brandt 2022 definition

issue: Min 22.5 is ~x4 too low (CTL plants run 100-150k USD/bpd -> 55-80 USD/GJ-yr); central 83 is on the low side of actuals.
benchmark: NETL 2009-2014 CTL: 100-150k USD/bpd -> ~75-110 CAD/GJ-per-yr
recommendation: Exclude 22.5 (Aranda?) or tag as nth-plant

issue: 1.3% of capex per year is below the 3-5% typical of gasification complexes.
benchmark: NETL: fixed O&M ~4% of TPC
recommendation: Check whether ETSAP fixed O&M excludes labour/maintenance

issue: LDAR is a recurring survey; a 1-1.5 yr 'capex' is really the annual survey cost. Treating it as capital with 1.5-yr life inflates the annuity and makes the measure look like equipment.
benchmark: ECCC 2018 RIAS: LDAR ~10-30 CAD/t CO2e, cost almost entirely recurring
recommendation: Store survey cost as opex-fixed per t CH4/yr; drop lifetime or set to programme life

issue: Max 1,908 is x56 the median; probably a per-site cost divided by a tiny single-leak quantity.
recommendation: Check the 1,908 example

value-in-db: 0.183 t/m3 bitumen vs SEC NG 3.4 + fuel 2.2 GJ/m3
issue: Fuel rows imply >=0.3 t/m3 (3.4 GJ NG x 0.05 + 2.2 GJ diesel x 0.07), 1.7x the stated total; either [fuel] 2.2 is the total (then NG 3.4 > total) or the emissions are too low.
benchmark: CERI 2018: mining+extraction ~35-45 kg CO2e/bbl = 0.22-0.28 t/m3
recommendation: Re-check Millington 2017/2018 carrier definitions; make [fuel] the total or exclude

issue: Mines use 0.1-0.2 GJ/m3 of electricity (mostly self-generated); zero means it is netted into the NG row.
benchmark: CERI: ~30-60 kWh/bbl
recommendation: Tag as 'on-site cogen included in NG'

issue: Max 256,189 is x1,000 the central (hot-tap equipment divided by a one-off saving); with n=4 it distorts the range and any mean.
benchmark: STAR LL: hot taps/inline inspection avoid blowdowns at near-zero incremental cost
recommendation: Exclude the 256,189 example or re-express per event

issue: Low for a liner programme: STAR cites USD 30-60/ft for liners, ~USD 200-300k per mile saving ~1-4 t/yr -> 50,000-150,000 USD/t-yr.
benchmark: EPA STAR PRO (plastic liners): >50,000 USD per t CH4/yr
recommendation: Re-check capacity (4.3 t/yr) vs length lined

issue: High-bleed (15-20 scf/h) to low-bleed (1-6 scf/h) is 70-90%; 97% is a zero-bleed/instrument-air figure.
benchmark: ICF 2015: low-bleed 80-90%; zero-bleed 100%
recommendation: Use ~85%

issue: Central at max; the 1.4% example is a facility-level share, not a per-component reduction.
recommendation: Exclude 1.4; 89 per replaced component is fine

issue: x30-50 low: STAR reports plunger lift avoids 600-1,200 Mcf/yr per well (12-24 t CH4). The small denominator inflates capex (45,709 CAD/t-yr) and opex (7,646) by the same factor.
benchmark: EPA STAR LL (plunger lift): USD 2.6-10k per well, 600-1,200 Mcf/yr saved -> 200-800 USD/t-yr
recommendation: Re-extract STAR LL example; expected capex ~500-1,000 CAD/t-per-yr

issue: Annualized (10 yr, 5%) gives ~13,500 CAD/t CH4 = ~540 CAD/t CO2e, 8x the archetype's own abatement-cost central (66); internally inconsistent.
benchmark: Dunsky 2023: 66 CAD/t CO2e
recommendation: Fix capacity (see above); then capex ~1,000 CAD/t-yr

issue: = 25,000-45,000 USD/bpd, the pre-2010 design estimates; built GTL plants cost 100,000+ USD/bpd (Oryx ~35k, Pearl ~100-150k, Escravos ~300k).
benchmark: Actuals 100-150k USD/bpd -> 60-90 CAD/GJ-per-yr
recommendation: Add a post-2012 example; tag ETSAP as design estimate

issue: Central at min; ETSAP gives 30 and process plants of this scale run 25-30 yr.
= 132 kg/bbl, at the top of upgrading intensities; consistent only if it includes H2 production and coke combustion. NG 4.16 + fuel 2.83 GJ/m3 imply ~0.37 t/m3 from fuel.
benchmark: CERI/Nduagu: upgrading 60-130 kg CO2/bbl SCO
recommendation: Tag as including H2 plant + coke; check NG/fuel overlap (NG includes H2 feed)

issue: Natural gas 0.271 GJ/m3 gives 0.014 t/m3 - 9x less than the emissions central; either the SEC is missing fuel/electricity or the emissions include upstream.
benchmark: 0.126 t/m3 needs ~2.2 GJ/m3 fuel
recommendation: Re-check Nduagu 2017 SEC carriers; add [fuel]

issue: x1,000 error: preheat fuel per GJ of expander electricity is ~1-2 GJ/GJ (preheat to offset JT cooling), not ~1,000.
benchmark: Worrell 2015 / Joshi 2022: line-heater duty ~ 1-1.5 x generated power
recommendation: Re-check units (MJ vs GJ, or kWh)

issue: Expander isentropic efficiency is 80-88%; 96 is a generator/gearbox figure.
benchmark: GPSA: turboexpander 80-85% isentropic
recommendation: Tag as generator efficiency or use ~85

issue: Two tags for the same flow (SAGD fuel is natural gas); [fuel] < [natural-gas] so they are not a total/part pair. Same pattern in well_solvent-assisted (4.4 vs 4.89) and mine_open-pit.
benchmark: SOR 2.5-3 x ~2.9 GJ fuel per m3 steam = 7-9 GJ/m3
recommendation: Collapse to one carrier; 7.5 GJ/m3 is the right order

issue: RECs are per completion event (~10 MMcf = ~190 t each); 4.1 kt/yr is a fleet or programme total, not one unit, so the per-t capex (240) may be a programme average.
benchmark: STAR LL: ~USD 30k per completion, 190-300 t CH4 saved
recommendation: State basis (per completion vs per programme)

issue: Black liquor input per t black liquor solids cannot exceed the HHV of the solids; 34.6 GJ/t is 2.5x the fuel's heating value. The IEAGHG 2016 example is almost certainly per ADt pulp (its reference mill is 800 kADt/yr; 1.5–1.8 t BLS/ADt x 14 GJ/t = 21–25 GJ/ADt) or per t pulp on another basis.
benchmark: HHV of kraft black liquor solids 13–15 GJ/t (Adams/Vakkilainen; PP BREF 2015 12.5–14.5 MJ/kg)
recommendation: Re-base the IEAGHG 2016 example to t BLS (divide by t BLS/ADt) or exclude it; keep the 15.7 example as central

issue: 2.4 t CO2/t BLS implies 65% carbon in the solids; black liquor is ~33–36% C. The 2.4 example is per ADt pulp (1.6 t BLS/ADt x 1.3 = 2.1–2.4).
benchmark: Stoichiometric: 0.34 kg C/kg BLS -> 1.2–1.3 t CO2/t BLS (biogenic)
recommendation: Re-base or exclude the 2.4 example; central 1.11–1.3 is right

issue: Minimum of 10% is not a boiler thermal efficiency; it is an electrical or power-only efficiency pooled with steam-raising efficiency.
benchmark: Recovery boiler steam efficiency 62–72% HHV (Vakkilainen 2005); electrical efficiency of a kraft mill CHP 8–12%
recommendation: Exclude the 10% example or move it to efficiency [electric]

issue: Steam used by the boiler itself (sootblowing, air preheat, liquor heating) is ~10–12% of its ~10 GJ/t BLS steam output; 1.23 is at the top of that but defensible. Check that this is own-use and not net output.
benchmark: Sootblowing 2–3% + air/liquor preheat ~5–8% of steam raised (Vakkilainen)
recommendation: Confirm the steam tag means own consumption, not steam produced

issue: Exceeds the heating value of black liquor solids (13–15 GJ/t); the Francis 2002 value is per ADt pulp (1.5 t BLS/ADt x 14 = 21 GJ/ADt exactly).
benchmark: HHV of BLS 13–15 GJ/t
recommendation: Divide by the source's t BLS per ADt (about 1.5) or set to 14 GJ/t BLS by definition

issue: Steam of 5.9 GJ per t BLS with 0.351 t CO2 captured per t implies 17 GJ/t CO2, 4–6x any amine process. The IEAGHG 2016 figures are per ADt pulp with 90% capture (1.85 t CO2/ADt x 3.2 GJ/t CO2 = 5.9 GJ/ADt), so the whole IEAGHG example is on a different basis from the archetype.
benchmark: Post-combustion amine reboiler duty 2.5–4 GJ/t CO2 (IEAGHG 2016, IEA 2020)
recommendation: Re-base the IEAGHG example to t BLS (divide by ~1.6–1.8 t BLS/ADt) and make capture and steam consistent; or move the energy to the diffuse-capture service as the desc says

issue: Central is a partial-capture case (32% share) while the archetype is a capture option a model would expect at ~90%; the 1.85 example is per ADt pulp (0.9 x 2.1 t CO2/ADt). The three examples are on different capture shares and product bases.
benchmark: Recovery boiler CO2 1.2–1.3 t/t BLS; 90% capture -> 1.1–1.2 t/t BLS
recommendation: Split into a 90%-capture value per t BLS; exclude or re-base the per-ADt example; align share-to-capture

issue: With 0.351 t CO2/t captured this is 2.5 GJ (700 kWh) per t CO2, 5x compression plus auxiliaries. Consistent only with the per-ADt, 90%-capture basis (0.888/1.85 = 0.48 GJ/t CO2).
benchmark: Capture + compression electricity 0.35–0.55 GJ/t CO2 (100–150 kWh/t)
recommendation: Re-base with the steam figure; present both per t CO2 captured

issue: 800 kt/yr is the IEAGHG reference mill's pulp output (ADt), not black liquor solids; confirms the example is per ADt.
benchmark: IEAGHG 2016/TR9 reference kraft mill 800 kADt/yr
recommendation: Convert to t BLS (~1.3–1.4 Mt/yr) or drop

issue: Displacement (RDH/SuperBatch) batch cooking recovers most cooking heat and uses 1.5–2.5 GJ/ADt; 3.2–5.1 GJ/ADt is conventional batch cooking without displacement, so the values belong to the legacy batch digester, not the archetype described.
benchmark: PP BREF 2015: conventional batch 3.5–4.5 GJ/ADt, displacement batch 1.4–2.2 GJ/ADt; continuous 1.6–2.7
recommendation: Either rename the archetype to conventional batch or re-extract displacement-batch values (NRCan 2008 best-practice column)

issue: 150–200 kWh/ADt is 3x the digester's own electricity; likely includes chip handling, washing and screening.
benchmark: Digester electricity 40–70 kWh/ADt (PP BREF 2015 cooking 50–75 kWh/ADt incl. washing)
recommendation: Check scope of the NRCan 2008 line; accept if it is cooking + washing

issue: The 3,869 example is a whole greenfield kraft mill (2,000–3,000 USD/ADt-yr), not a digester; 14x the other example.
benchmark: Greenfield kraft mill 2,000–3,000 USD/ADt-yr (Suzano/Arauco projects); continuous digester 150–300 M USD per 1 Mt/yr = 200–400 CAD/t-yr
recommendation: Exclude the 3,869 example from the digester; keep 268

issue: Untagged total is 4x the sum of steam (1.97) and electricity (0.158); the 18.5 example is whole-mill total energy (incl. black liquor) and 8.79 is likely whole-mill purchased energy.
benchmark: Digester total 1.8–2.9 GJ/ADt; whole kraft mill 14–20 GJ/ADt total, 4–8 GJ/ADt purchased
recommendation: Exclude the whole-mill examples; set total = steam + electricity (~2.1 GJ/ADt)

issue: A digester has no meaningful conversion efficiency; the ETSAP I07 90% is a generic figure assigned to several pulp archetypes (also paper machine, RCF, TMP).
recommendation: Drop the ETSAP I07 efficiency from unit-process pulp archetypes

issue: 580–620 kWh/ADt is a whole NSSC pulping line (cooking plus refining), not a digester; acceptable only if the archetype is defined as the whole pulping line.
benchmark: NSSC pulping 400–650 kWh/t incl. refining (US DOE bandwidth 2015); cooking alone <100 kWh/t
recommendation: Make the desc say whole semi-chemical pulping line, or split refining out

issue: 4.4 GJ/t (1,220 kWh/ADt) exceeds a whole sulphite mill's electricity; central is far above digester-only values.
benchmark: Sulphite cooking 50–100 kWh/ADt; whole sulphite mill 600–900 kWh/ADt (PP BREF 2015)
recommendation: Check the 4.4 example; probably whole mill or MJ/kg confusion; use 0.46 for the digester

issue: Product unit is 't water evaporated or t product'; the range spans both bases (per t water evaporated 2.8–3.5 GJ/t; per t paper 4–7 GJ/t). The pooled median mixes them.
benchmark: Latent heat 2.26 GJ/t water + losses = 2.8–3.5 GJ/t water (BREF dryer 1.2–1.5 kg steam/kg water); paper machine drying 4–7 GJ/t paper
recommendation: Fix one product basis (t paper is what the model needs) and re-base the per-water examples at ~1.1–1.3 t water/t paper

issue: CO2e is twice the CO2 from the same source (0.15); combustion CH4/N2O add <2%, so the UKERC co2e includes something else (electricity or whole-mill scope).
benchmark: CO2e/CO2 ratio for gas or biomass combustion 1.00–1.02
recommendation: Re-check UKERC 2013 scope; drop the co2e line or make both consistent

issue: 1,170–2,230 CAD per t/yr is a whole paper machine (or more); the dryer section is 30–40% of machine cost.
benchmark: New paper machine 1,000–1,500 USD/t-yr; dryer section 300–600 CAD/t-yr
recommendation: Confirm Martin 2000 scope; label as whole machine or scale by ~0.35

issue: 1.9 GJ/t (530 kWh/t) is the whole paper machine's electricity, not the dryer section (hood fans, drives ~50–100 kWh/t).
benchmark: Dryer section 50–100 kWh/t; whole machine 400–700 kWh/t
recommendation: Exclude the 1.9 example

issue: An efficiency variant should sit below the base; base dryer_steam-heated total is 4.02 (steam 3.4) and the strong variant 4.19. The CT 2011 values are whole dryer per t paper, the base is a mix of bases, so the ladder is inverted.
benchmark: Base dryer section 4–6 GJ/t paper; moderate measures −10%, strong −20–25%
recommendation: Put base and variants on one source/basis (CT 2011 base case ~5.4 GJ/t?) so moderate < base and strong < moderate

issue: Incremental efficiency measures priced at 1,400 CAD/t-yr equals a new dryer section; CT 2011 gives whole-dryer cost with measures, not the increment.
benchmark: Dryer-section efficiency retrofits (hood closure, heat recovery, condensate) 20–80 CAD/t-yr
recommendation: Treat as whole-dryer capex (compare with base 1,657) or extract the increment

issue: Above the base archetype's 4.02 GJ/t; see moderate row.
benchmark: Strong measures should be 20–25% below base
recommendation: Rebase with the moderate variant

issue: Moderate variant 20 years, strong 10 years from the same CT 2011 source; probably a measure-life vs equipment-life mix.
benchmark: Dryer section 20–30 years; measure life 10–15
recommendation: Use one lifetime convention for the ladder

issue: Central is the top of a 2x range; 21.6 + 9 GJ/t electricity = 30.6 GJ/t tissue is at the extreme of TAD literature.
benchmark: PP BREF 2015 TAD: 2,000–3,000 kWh/t electricity, 10–16 GJ/t thermal (about 2x conventional 5.5–7 GJ/t)
recommendation: Use midpoint (~15 GJ/t) or check whether 21.6 includes Yankee + TAD

issue: Heat (5.6) is 2.4x the steam central (2.3) for the same duty; the BREF value is probably total mill drying + evaporation or a flash-dryer figure.
benchmark: Pulp dryer 2.3–3.2 GJ/ADt steam (PP BREF 2015 drying 2.5–3 GJ/ADt)
recommendation: Drop the heat tag or merge into steam with the lower value

issue: 7 Mt/yr black liquor solids would be a 19,000 tds/d evaporator; the IEAGHG value is t water evaporated per year (the 800 kADt mill produces ~1.4 Mt BLS and evaporates ~6–7 Mt water).
benchmark: Largest kraft evaporator trains ~1,500–2,000 t water/h = 5–7 Mt/yr water
recommendation: Re-base capacity to t BLS (divide by ~4.5–5 t water/t BLS)

issue: Per t BLS this gives only ~24 M CAD for a 1.4 Mt BLS/yr train; per t water evaporated it gives ~120 M CAD, which is the right order, so capex is on the water basis like the capacity.
benchmark: 7-effect evaporator train for a 1 Mt ADt mill 80–150 M USD = ~110–200 CAD/t BLS-yr
recommendation: Multiply by t water/t BLS (~4.5–5) to put on the archetype basis; same for opex-fixed

issue: Values of 3.5–4.5 are the usual per-ADt evaporation figures; per t BLS (1.6 t BLS/ADt) they are 2.2–2.8 GJ/t. Per-ADt and per-t-BLS examples are pooled.
benchmark: PP BREF 2015 evaporation 3.5–4.5 GJ/ADt = 2.2–2.8 GJ/t BLS; 6–7 effects ~0.45 GJ/t water
recommendation: Check each example's basis; the untagged 2.36 (DOE 2015) is likely the correct per-t-BLS figure

issue: Untagged total is lower than the steam-only central (3.66); the two sources are on different bases.
benchmark: Total = steam + 0.1 electricity
recommendation: Reconcile with the steam row

issue: 8,368 CAD/t-yr is 15x the other example and above a whole greenfield mill; it is either per t/day or a whole-mill BLGCC plant cost mis-divided.
benchmark: BLGCC plant 300–500 M USD for 1,500–2,000 tds/d (Larson 2006) = 600–1,100 CAD/t BLS-yr
recommendation: Exclude or re-derive the 8,368 example

issue: Range mixes a fraction stored as percent (0.179), electrical efficiency (~15–25%) and cold-gas/fuel efficiency (~50–56%). Central of 15% is an electrical efficiency while the carrier-tagged efficiencies (50–60%) are cold-gas efficiencies.
benchmark: BLG cold-gas efficiency 50–60% (Ekbom 2003); BLGCC net electrical efficiency 18–25%
recommendation: Split into efficiency [electric] and efficiency [cold-gas]; fix the 0.179 unit

issue: Exceeds the HHV of black liquor solids; the Ekbom 2003 value is per ADt pulp (about 1.7 t BLS/ADt x 14 GJ/t).
